commenti.body:
So the start was boring for you, the final third (supernatural stuff) you didn’t enjoy.

I can confirm with you that you did not enjoy the film.

Personally I thought the film looked very nice, had good performances and I loved the tone and tension of the first half. Second half I thought was pretty bad.

I also did not find it very scary and the marketing/hype incredibly misleading.

I’ll admit I have forced myself to forget a lot of it because I found it to be not very good in the end.

I thought it was pretty bad save for the first forty minutes. I thought the supernatural aspect and the whole “devil” angle was pretty terrible and a cop out of what could have maybe been an interesting film. 

Why does the devil need a woman to get dolls to get him souls of little girls or something? I thought it was a pretty pretentious amount of all style and no substance. Im also a pretty big fan of nicholas cage but I thought this was just too much. I was laughing when he was on acreen and not because I was nervous, but because it was just ridiculous. I think he’s a brilliant actor but that doesnt mean he shouldn’t be reigned in every once in a while.

Normally there are a lot of things I can forgive in a film but my issues with the film began to pile up around the halfway point. I almost fell asleep but then ny wife woke me up, I wish she hadn’t.

I remember being positive on it but vaguely disappointed the first time I watched it. I chalk this up to the marketing making it sound like the scariest thing in the world, when it really was more building a quiet dread.

I rewatched it recently and actually LOVED it with more proper expectations. I found it to be an extremely well-executed combination of a detective thriller with weird horror fiction. What it basically results in is a detective movie in which you feel like you’re learning more details about the case in every scene, but at the same time the details you’re learning are only raising more questions, and those questions continually alter the stakes of things. This essentially leads to an experience where you spend the entire movie kind of confused and kind of unsettled, and combined with really effective imagery, performances and dialogue, it creates a really unique and suspenseful film. 

That being said, it’s not for everyone, and as someone else in the thread pointed out it really sounds like it might just not have been something you liked at all. But that’s just my pitch for what really makes the film work for me.

Now I’m not usually one to harp about “stealing”, but Longlegs took a ton from The Exorcist 3. Like, nearly its entire plot. I was pretty confused by some of the elements in Longlegs, especially the ending which I felt was kind of inconclusive, but watching TE3 made a lot clear.

This was one of my most hyped films of 24, and honestly I thought it was pretty awful from beginning to end. Looked great. Like the overall atmosphere. But personally I thought only really Maika Monroe's performance was any good. Nic Cage was taking swings like Nic Cage will do, but his performance felt like parody and as if the director didn't even try to rein him in. It was a poorly written film that was most poorly executed. Again, dug the atmosphere but it just wasn't the movie that was sold in my opinion and the movie that was sold would have been far better. The moment you start throwing around all time greats like Se7en and Silence of the Lambs like the director and marketing did, you really raise the bar and imo they did themselves no favors with the comparisons because this wasn't even in the same stratosphere.
I’ve not actually seen the exorcist 3, but i have been meaning to watch it for a while. Out of interest what did they steal from it?

I was VERY excited prior to its release and was VERY disappointed after seeing it on opening night. Oz Perkins is an amazing visual director (i thought his blocking in Longlegs was Spielberg-level shit) and he did a good job at establishing a bleak/tense tone, but he makes for a dumb writer imo. The idea to make Longlegs be a servant of the devil and have supernatural abilities by being able to create satanic dolls that make fathers kill their families felt like a cheap cop-out more than anything. Probably my fault for expecting a movie to be anything before watching it, but I really did expect it to be smarter. Stupid ending and the "hail satan :D (cut to credits" shit made my eyes roll out of my head. Great needledrops though, been listening to that Dinosaur Jr. song since I first saw it.

I liked it, my only issue is Nicolas Cage was too Nicolas Cage, I wish he would have gone deeper into character since the makeup was so good. There were too many instances where I was aware that it was Nicolas Cage acting. It would have been such a great opportunity for him to dig deep and do more of a character performance where you can’t tell it’s him. Like, no matter how much I tell myself it’s Heath Ledger playing Joker I can’t ever see him in the character.

I went to see it with a friend and she had the same opinion as some of the comments here. Idk for me it was awesome, that atmosphere really got me spooked and I loved that is was so Alan Wake vibes. And Cage, oh man, his performance gave me nightmares. 
I was also excited for this movie so I tried to stay away from any review, trailer or even images prior to see it. Ive noticed how the "best horror film of the year/decade/month" comments always ruin my experience

Kind of the entire plot (a satanic killer using possessions to kill people), but the ending specifically is essentially lifted directly from TE3. Interestingly, the scene that was used as the ending in longlegs isn’t actually the ending of TE3, which is probably why it feels so open ended.

[This literary analysis of the movie will probably help you make sense of it.](https://filmcolossus.com/longlegs-explained-2024)

Oz Perkins went on record and said that the FBI stuff and supernatural stuff was just to get people into the seats. The only thing he was interested in was the dynamic between the mom and daughter and the lie.

So he went through the motions with a lot of the story. Which is what gives the movie such a strange energy.
Makes a lot of sense. Thanks for sharing!
